2609.38028.title: doPlan: A Variable-Horizon Dataset for Multi-Stage Language-Conditioned Planning in Autonomous Driving
2609.38028.paper_summary: Autonomous vehicles interacting with passengers through natural language must reason beyond immediate commands. Passenger intent may span multiple stages of behavior, depend on future events, refer to surrounding agents or landmarks, and remain relevant as driving conditions evolve. Existing language-enabled driving datasets largely focus on short, localized interactions, leaving these longer-horizon forms of passenger intent comparatively underexplored. We introduce doPlan, to our knowledge the first publicly available, human-annotated real-world dataset designed to study passenger language as persistent task context. Built on nuPlan, doPlan contains 5,154 human-written passenger instructions spanning 169.1 hours of cumulative instruction-aligned context over 50.9 hours of unique driving, with annotation windows ranging from 30.0 to 508.8 s. The annotations capture immediate, deferred, event-conditioned, persistent, and multi-stage passenger intent. The dataset, annotation interface, and supporting resources are publicly available at https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/doPlan. We evaluate four language-conditioned driving models and find that sensitivity to passenger language does not reliably translate into behavior consistent with the requested direction. More broadly, among 2,161 examples with a matched future maneuver, the first associated maneuver occurs a median of 24.6 s after the evaluation point, and only 9.8% occur within the models' common 5 s prediction horizon. These findings highlight the need to connect persistent passenger intent with successive planning decisions. doPlan provides a setting for studying how unresolved goals can be retained, grounded in evolving scenes, and tracked across multiple stages, including how a planner determines when a future goal becomes relevant to the current plan.
2609.38028.paper_summary_zh: 自主車輛通過自然語言與乘客互動時，必須超越即時命令進行推理。乘客的意圖可能跨越多個行為階段，依賴未來事件，參考周圍的代理或地標，並在駕駛條件演變時保持相關性。現有的語言驅動駕駛數據集主要集中在短期、局部的互動上，這使得這些較長期的乘客意圖形式相對未被充分探索。我們介紹了 doPlan，據我們所知，這是第一個公開可用的人類標註的真實世界數據集，旨在研究乘客語言作為持續任務上下文。doPlan 基於 nuPlan，包含 5,154 條人類撰寫的乘客指令，涵蓋 169.1 小時的累積指令對齊上下文，並在 50.9 小時的獨特駕駛中，標註窗口範圍從 30.0 到 508.8 秒。這些標註捕捉了即時、延遲、事件條件、持續和多階段的乘客意圖。該數據集、標註介面和支持資源可在 https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/doPlan 上公開獲得。我們評估了四個語言條件的駕駛模型，發現對乘客語言的敏感性並不可靠地轉化為與請求方向一致的行為。更廣泛地說，在 2,161 個與未來動作匹配的例子中，第一個相關動作的發生中位數為評估點後 24.6 秒，且只有 9.8% 發生在模型的常見 5 秒預測範圍內。這些發現凸顯了將持續乘客意圖與後續規劃決策相連接的必要性。doPlan 提供了一個研究如何保留未解決目標的環境，這些目標根植於不斷演變的場景中，並在多個階段中進行跟蹤，包括規劃者如何確定未來目標何時與當前計劃相關。
